raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`HiCacheFile` (the `file` L3 storage backend) reads one page file at a time on each rank's single prefetch I/O thread (`open` + `readinto` per page). On a node-local NVMe tier with large prompts this serializes restores: in our tests (MiMo-V2.6-Pro, TP4 on B300, `--hicache-storage-backend file`) a rank read ~1.3 GB/s single-threaded, and when many sessions resumed at once loads queued until prefetches timed out and fell back to recompute.

The existing multi-I/O-worker work (#31440 / #31797) parallelizes whole operations, which can reorder them across ranks. This change only parallelizes the file reads *inside one* `batch_get` / `batch_get_v2` call and returns after all of them, so operation order across ranks is unchanged.

## Modifications

- New env `SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_READ_WORKERS` (default `1` = current behaviour), documented in `environment_variables.mdx`.
- `HiCacheFile._map_reads`: runs the reads of one call on a lazily created `ThreadPoolExecutor`, waits for all of them, keeps input order; a read that raises becomes a miss (`None` / `False`) instead of failing the batch.
- `batch_get` uses it; `_batch_io_v2` (used by `batch_get_v2`) reads pages into private staging pages on the pool, chunked (4 × workers), while every `set_from_flat_data_page` stays on the calling thread in page order. That last point matters: a unified host pool takes a thread-local layout lease in `set_from_flat_data_page` and the caller already holds it for the whole transfer; our first version wrote pages from pool threads and deadlocked (a pool thread with lease depth 0 waited for a pending compaction, which waited for the I/O thread's lease → one rank's prefetch ack never arrived).
- Writes (`batch_set*`) stay serial.
- New CPU test `test/registered/hicache/test_hicache_file_parallel_reads.py`: parallel equals serial (bit-exact, same order), pool writes stay on the calling thread, a missing page is a miss, `batch_get` parallel equals serial, and reads really run on several threads (this one fails without the change).

## Accuracy Tests

No model code changes. With the same change on `lmsysorg/sglang:dev` (nightly 684fea8a), 8 workers, MiMo-V2.6-Pro on 4× B300: 0 hangs, 0 tracebacks, answers identical to a cold run after restores from disk (temperature 0), and ~14 h of reasoning benchmarks with the disk tier on afterwards without errors.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Honest numbers, measured on that setup (8 workers vs serial):
- raw read throughput of real page files per rank: 1.27 GB/s (1 thread) → 3.35 GB/s (8 threads);
- end-to-end restores: ~+25 % at 32 concurrent resumes of 56k-token prompts (30.3 s vs 37.9 s, all from disk), no gain for a few large ones (4 × 741k: 78.2 s vs 71.8 s). The file read stops being the main limit; what remains is serial (existence check, per-page staging copy, page-by-page `set_from_flat_data_page`).

So this is a modest, opt-in improvement for node-local storage, not a big win; it is off by default.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 as pinned)
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (The e2e `test_hicache_storage_file_backend.py` needs a GPU server and was not run locally.)
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Related: #44774 (flat pages for asymmetric K/V host pools, needed for the file backend on MiMo-V2; independent of this change).

@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+"""Parallel page reads in HiCacheFile (SGLANG_HICACHE_FILE_BACKEND_READ_WORKERS).
+
+With read_workers > 1, batch_get and batch_get_v2 read the page files of one call
+on a thread pool. The results must be identical to serial reads, in the same
+order; a read that fails must become a miss, not fail the batch; and every
+host-pool write (set_from_flat_data_page) must stay on the calling thread,
+because host pools may hold thread-local state there (calling it from a pool
+thread can deadlock with a unified host pool's layout lease).
+
+CPU-only: a minimal flat-page host pool over a CPU tensor and the real
+HiCacheFile backend.
+"""
+
+import tempfile
+import threading
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_storage import (
+    HiCacheFile,
+    HiCacheStorageConfig,
+    PoolName,
+    PoolTransfer,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+PAGE_SIZE, PAGE_NUMEL, PAGES = 4, 1024, 24
+
+
+class _FlatPagePool:
+    """The flat-page subset of a host pool that HiCacheFile uses."""
+
+    def __init__(self, fill: bool):
+        self.page_size = PAGE_SIZE
+        self.buffer = (
+            torch.randn(PAGES, PAGE_NUMEL) if fill else torch.zeros(PAGES, PAGE_NUMEL)
+        )
+        self.write_threads = set()
+
+    def get_data_page(self, index, flat: bool = True):
+        return self.buffer[index // PAGE_SIZE].clone()
+
+    def get_dummy_flat_data_page(self):
+        return torch.zeros(PAGE_NUMEL)
+
+    def set_from_flat_data_page(self, index, data_page):
+        self.write_threads.add(threading.get_ident())
+        self.buffer[index // PAGE_SIZE].copy_(data_page)
+
+
+def _storage(path: str) -> HiCacheFile:
+    config = HiCacheStorageConfig(
+        tp_rank=0,
+        tp_size=1,
+        pp_rank=0,
+        pp_size=1,
+        attn_cp_rank=0,
+        attn_cp_size=1,
+        is_mla_model=False,
+        enable_storage_metrics=False,
+        is_page_first_layout=True,
+        model_name="test",
+        extra_config={"file_storage_path": path},
+    )
+    return HiCacheFile(config)
+
+
+def _transfer(keys, pages):
+    host_indices = torch.tensor(
+        [p * PAGE_SIZE + i for p in pages for i in range(PAGE_SIZE)]
+    )
+    return PoolTransfer(name=PoolName.KV, keys=keys, host_indices=host_indices)
+
+
+class TestHiCacheFileParallelReads(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.path = tempfile.mkdtemp()
+        writer = _storage(self.path)
+        self.src = _FlatPagePool(fill=True)
+        writer.register_mem_host_pool_v2(self.src, PoolName.KV)
+        self.keys = [f"page-{p}" for p in range(PAGES)]
+        written = writer.batch_set_v2([_transfer(self.keys, range(PAGES))])
+        self.assertEqual(written[PoolName.KV], [True] * PAGES)
+
+    def _read_v2(self, workers: int, keys):
+        storage = _storage(self.path)
+        storage.read_workers = workers
+        dst = _FlatPagePool(fill=False)
+        storage.register_mem_host_pool_v2(dst, PoolName.KV)
+        pages = list(reversed(range(len(keys))))  # restore into other slots
+        result = storage.batch_get_v2([_transfer(keys, pages)])[PoolName.KV]
+        return result, dst, pages
+
+    def test_parallel_equals_serial(self):
+        serial, serial_dst, pages = self._read_v2(1, self.keys)
+        parallel, parallel_dst, _ = self._read_v2(8, self.keys)
+        self.assertEqual(serial, [True] * PAGES)
+        self.assertEqual(parallel, serial)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(parallel_dst.buffer, serial_dst.buffer))
+        for i, page in enumerate(pages):
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(parallel_dst.buffer[page], self.src.buffer[i]))
+
+    def test_pool_writes_stay_on_calling_thread(self):
+        _, dst, _ = self._read_v2(8, self.keys)
+        self.assertEqual(dst.write_threads, {threading.get_ident()})
+
+    def test_reads_run_on_several_threads(self):
+        storage = _storage(self.path)
+        storage.read_workers = 4
+        storage.register_mem_host_pool_v2(_FlatPagePool(fill=False), PoolName.KV)
+        read_threads = set()
+        barrier = threading.Barrier(2, timeout=5)
+        original_get = storage.get
+
+        def get(key, target_location=None, target_sizes=None):
+            read_threads.add(threading.get_ident())
+            if len(read_threads) <= 2:
+                try:
+                    barrier.wait()  # two reads in flight at the same time
+                except threading.BrokenBarrierError:
+                    pass
+            return original_get(key, target_location, target_sizes)
+
+        storage.get = get
+        storage.batch_get_v2([_transfer(self.keys, range(PAGES))])
+        self.assertGreater(len(read_threads), 1)
+        self.assertNotIn(threading.get_ident(), read_threads)
+
+    def test_missing_page_is_a_miss(self):
+        keys = list(self.keys)
+        keys[5] = "not-stored"
+        result, _, _ = self._read_v2(8, keys)
+        self.assertFalse(result[5])
+        self.assertEqual(sum(result), PAGES - 1)
+
+    def test_batch_get_parallel_equals_serial(self):
+        for workers in (1, 8):
+            storage = _storage(self.path)
+            storage.read_workers = workers
+            targets = [torch.zeros(PAGE_NUMEL) for _ in self.keys]
+            got = storage.batch_get(self.keys, targets)
+            for i, page in enumerate(got):
+                self.assertIsNotNone(page)
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(page, self.src.buffer[i]))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
